EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a classic para-disubstituted benzene fingerprint: very strong ring C–H out-of-plane band at 840 cm⁻¹ together with companion bands at 810 and 708 cm⁻¹. 1622 cm⁻¹ (medium) is the aromatic C=C stretch, and the pair 3022 / 3073 cm⁻¹ are aromatic C–H stretches. Aliphatic C–H stretches at 2956 and 2845 cm⁻¹ plus a prominent CH₂ wag at 1171 cm⁻¹ indicate a benzylic –CH₂– group, not a methoxy –OCH₃. The intense 1276 cm⁻¹ band matches the C–O stretch of a benzylic alcohol. Crucially, two medium bands at 645 and 535 cm⁻¹ fall in the typical C–Cl stretching region (Nakamoto rule GFQ-041), supporting a chloro-substituent; no strong C–F stretch (~1100 cm⁻¹) is observed. Among the candidates, only OCc1ccc(Cl)cc1 (para-chlorobenzyl alcohol) possesses (1) a para-Cl substituent, (2) a benzylic CH₂OH group, and (3) an aromatic ring, accounting coherently for all key bands. Therefore it best fits the experimental Raman peaks.
